intro_html: The soda cooks off and leaves behind a sweet, caramel-like depth that makes this pulled pork taste like a backyard cookout. Piled over potatoes, each bowl carries 56 grams of protein for around $2.58 (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings from one pot is barbecue money well spent.
cost_closing_html: About $2.58 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each serving lands near 557 calories with 56 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Sweet, smoky, and stupid easy. This one always disappears fast. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Use zero-sugar soda to get the caramelized flavor without the extra sugar and calories. It works just as well as the regular stuff.
A sugar-free BBQ sauce keeps the carbs down while still giving you that tangy, smoky finish.
Potatoes are your cheapest base by far. A 9 lb bag under $9 stretches this whole batch and then some.
make_it: Set the pork loin in the slow cooker and scatter the sliced onion around it.
Pour the zero-sugar soda over the pork until it is about halfway up the sides.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork shreds easily.
Drain off most of the liquid, then shred the pork right in the pot.
Stir in the BBQ sauce and let it warm through for a few minutes.
Serve over cooked potatoes and divide into containers.
